translations.t0063: Audit decompression behaviour in bulk copy jobs
translations.t0064: The job did not account for on-write decompression; the first run failed due to a full target device — an unexpected failure pattern that could have triggered an alert.
translations.t0065: The first run failed at approximately 40% fill level; the perpetrator deleted a snapshot (~9.1 TB) and restarted the job — a total of approximately 6.5 hours of activity on scratch-02.
translations.t0066: Send automatic alerts for unexpected errors on scratch arrays (job aborts, sudden free-space jumps caused by snapshot deletions) to an on-call team in real time; define thresholds for unusually large snapshot deletions.
translations.t0067: Anomalous events (job failures, 9 TB snapshot deletion) become visible even when no complete audit log is present.
translations.t0068: Alerting systems must be independent of the logging window, otherwise they share the same vulnerability. Too many false alarms can lead to alert fatigue. Conditional recommendation, as it is unclear whether a separate monitoring system was in place.
translations.t0069: Had such monitoring been active, the job failure at approximately 02:00 and the snapshot deletion at 02:41 would have triggered an alarm — in the middle of the time of the offence.
translations.t0070: Caduff claims he started the eval sweep remotely via VPN from home — a VPN log could establish that only a remote read-only login actually took place and that no local session occurred on the engineering floor.
translations.t0071: Caduff says he was in St. Gallen: Friday at home, Saturday climbing gym, Sunday dinner at a friend's. Card transactions or receipts could corroborate his presence in St. Gallen.
translations.t0072: Caduff has no car — the garage log could indirectly confirm that no vehicle registered to him appears, and rule out that he entered the building via the underground garage.
translations.t0073: For the offence, the key question is whether Caduff knew which bundles are genuine. He denies having read the Confluence page or seen the board deck — other sources could confirm or refute this.
translations.t0074: A Slack entry shows Caduff reporting the return of a portable array with intact seals in September — this documents legitimate handling of such devices and could explain why his name is associated with portable arrays.
translations.t0075: Written confirmation from Hofer for the checkpoint accesses is absent. A follow-up protocol or note could independently corroborate the authorisation and explain S1 (notably high accesses) as legitimate.
translations.t0076: 31 checkpoint accesses in four weeks (company median: 2); VPN eval sweep started at 22:05 CEST on the Friday of the offence — precisely on the night without audit logging.
translations.t0077: Research line closed, role ends August 2026; Caduff describes himself as an ideal perpetrator profile: motive, access, no alibi.
translations.t0078: No independently verifiable alibi for the night of the offence: alone in his flat in St. Gallen.
translations.t0079: Knows the undocumented current staging path (K2) and has deep knowledge of checkpoint structure.
translations.t0080: No personal vehicle; how the physical device would have been transported remains open.
translations.t0081: The 31 accesses are fully explained by research explicitly authorised verbally by Lukas Hofer for a methods paper of his own. The authorisation is documented threefold via calendar, Slack DM, and Hofer's follow-up interview. Hofer also confirms that eval sweeps by Caduff occurred routinely in October and are technically read-only, without coming near the scratch arrays for writes.
translations.t0082: Meeting note documents the verbal authorisation of 02.10.2025.
translations.t0083: Caduff's thank-you message the following day confirms the arrangement and shows he was aware of the conditions.
translations.t0084: Hofer explicitly confirms the authorisation in the follow-up interview.
translations.t0085: Hofer confirms that eval sweeps in October were routine and technically perform no write operations on scratch arrays.
translations.t0086: Hofer reviewed the network billing records after the Kestrel preprint and found no indication of a terabyte-scale transfer over VPN on the night of the offence.
translations.t0087: Caduff acknowledges the motive himself but argues persuasively that he would not have needed to steal the model intelligence because he can reconstruct the procedure from memory. This claim is not falsifiable, but is consistent with his role as Principal Research Engineer and with Hofer's assessment of his technical level.
translations.t0088: Caduff argues he would not have needed to steal the weights, as his knowledge resides in his head.
translations.t0089: Email from Dov Halperin confirms that the notice of termination was not intended pejoratively and that the role continues until August 2026.
translations.t0090: Caduff himself describes his profile as ideal for the perpetrator — the motive is real and persists.
translations.t0091: No independently verifiable alibi for the core time of the offence (23:10 CEST Friday to 05:58 CEST Saturday) exists. No card entry, no garage entry, and no witness statement places Caduff physically elsewhere or in the office during this window. His vehicle is absent from the garage log, which is consistent with the claim 'no car', but is not an alibi.
translations.t0092: Caduff has no car; the absence of his registration plate from the garage log is therefore to be expected and constitutes no positive corroboration of an alibi.
translations.t0093: Calendar entry documents a planned read-only sweep session from 22:00 CEST — it establishes the booking, not physical presence at home.
translations.t0094: No technical source can independently confirm or rule out Caduff's whereabouts during the night of the offence.
translations.t0095: Caduff's knowledge of the undocumented staging path (K2) is clearly established and undisputed. As regards decoy knowledge (K1), he denies having read the Confluence page or seen the board deck. However, he was on Iris Ammann's original list of five persons in the know. His statement that he only read the paths he had always read is consistent with the finding that no decoy was opened — but it is not proof.
translations.t0096: Caduff claims he knew the decoys by name, but not the specific real/decoy mapping by path.
translations.t0097: Caduff denies having read Yannick's Confluence page.
translations.t0098: Caduff denies having seen the board deck from February 2025.
translations.t0099: Caduff was on Iris Ammann's original list of five persons in the know for the decoy programme.
translations.t0100: Iris Ammann explicitly counts Caduff among the five persons who were to know the decoy programme — according to this source, he received direct knowledge of the real/decoy mapping.
translations.t0101: The absence of a personal vehicle makes physical transport of a large drive by car less likely, but does not exclude it: the alley door is, by Caduff's own account and per helpdesk tickets, chronically unsecured. A drive fits in a backpack or bicycle basket. The missing vehicle is not an alibi.
translations.t0102: Caduff has no car; no garage entry in his name exists.
translations.t0103: Helpdesk ticket shows Caduff attempted to open the alley door with his badge on multiple occasions — he was familiar with the entrance.
translations.t0104: Caduff himself identifies the simplest physical access route (alley door, no badge required) — which both establishes his knowledge of this route and includes every other potential perpetrator.
translations.t0105: Caduff demonstrably has knowledge of K2 (undocumented staging path) and was on Iris Ammann's original list of five for K1 (real/decoy mapping). He denies having read the Confluence page or seen the board deck; that is not refutable, but he had a direct source for K1. Knowledge of K3 (decompression on write) is plausibly present in a Principal Research Engineer with four years working on these pipelines — Jira ticket SEC-486 ('Improve error message on decompress-on-write overflow') identifies him as a commenter, which establishes awareness of this phenomenon. Knowledge of K4 (logging window) was public knowledge to approximately 40 persons.
translations.t0106: Caduff had read access to the checkpoint tree via VPN. The exfiltration was carried out physically from a workstation console on the engineering floor — this requires physical presence. No badge log and no garage entry either establishes or rules out his presence. The alley door is, per multiple sources, chronically unsecured and accessible without a car. His remote sweep cannot have executed the local session (technically excluded per Hofer / network billing).
translations.t0107: The core time of the offence is 23:10 CEST (Friday) to 05:58 CEST (Saturday). Caduff's Slack message at 22:05 CEST establishes that he started a remote sweep at that time. No card entry, no witness, and no system log places him physically in St. Gallen or in the office during the night of the offence. Lukas Hofer subsequently reviewed the network billing records and found no TB-scale transfer over VPN — this exculpates the VPN sweep but says nothing about physical presence.
translations.t0108: Caduff was on Iris Ammann's original list of five and had direct knowledge of K1 (real/decoy mapping by path) — he denies this, but the source is unambiguous.
translations.t0109: No independent alibi for the physical night of the offence (23:10–05:58 CEST) exists. Absence of exculpatory evidence is not proof of guilt, but the case remains open.
translations.t0110: Caduff commented on ticket SEC-486 ('decompress-on-write overflow') in September 2025, indicating awareness of the technical K3 detail that, according to Lukas Hofer himself, is often unknown even to experienced engineers.
translations.t0111: The legitimate accesses (S1) are well documented and exculpatory. The VPN sweep is technically separate from the physical exfiltration (network billing reviewed). No garage entry and no vehicle connect Caduff to the scene. However: he demonstrably possessed all three critical knowledge components (K1, K2, K3), has no physical alibi for the core time of the offence, and the exfiltration required physical presence that can be neither confirmed nor excluded.
translations.t0112: Andrin Caduff's high checkpoint access count is fully explained by research verbally authorised and subsequently confirmed by Lukas Hofer for a methods paper; the VPN sweep on the night of the offence is technically separate from the physical exfiltration and has been reviewed against the network billing. Nevertheless, the case remains open: Caduff demonstrably possessed all required knowledge components (real/decoy mapping, undocumented path, decompression behaviour), has no independently verifiable physical alibi for the core time of the offence, and no evidence rules out his physical presence in the building.
translations.t0113: Whether Caduff actually knew the real/decoy mapping (K1) or merely knew that decoys exist — his claim that he did not know is not falsifiable.
translations.t0114: No card entry, no transaction trail, and no witness physically establishes Caduff's whereabouts between approximately 22:05 CEST and Saturday morning.
